name: The Moralist
subtitle: Pascal, Pensées (selections, c. 8,000 words) and La Rochefoucauld, Maximes (selections, c. 4,000 words).
rationale: The distilled essence of French prose. Short, aphoristic, devastating. The moralist tradition from the seventeenth century. Introduces the philosophical vocabulary and the subjunctive in all its forms.
learning_outcomes: Read and translate selections from Pascal's Pensées.
Read and translate selections from La Rochefoucauld's Maximes.
Recognize the stylistic features of French moralist prose: brevity, paradox, antithesis.
Discuss the philosophical themes of each author in writing.
Translate any fifty-word passage from the chosen texts at sight.

texts.author: Blaise Pascal
texts.notes: Pascal's prose is dense, philosophical, and often paradoxical. The Pensées are fragments of a planned apology for Christianity, left unfinished at his death. The student will encounter the subjunctive, conditional sentences, and rhetorical questions.

texts.author: François de La Rochefoucauld
texts.notes: La Rochefoucauld's maxims are short, cynical observations on human nature. Each is a single sentence or two. The style is elegant, the vocabulary is precise, and the insight is cutting. The student will learn to read French at its most compressed.

vocabulary_focus: Philosophical terms: âme (soul), esprit (mind), cœur (heart), raison (reason)
Moralist vocabulary: vertu (virtue), vice, orgueil (pride), amour-propre (self-love)
Rhetorical structures: antithesis, paradox, rhetorical questions
grammar_focus: The subjunctive in clauses of doubt and necessity
Complex sentence structures with multiple subordinate clauses

sample_passages.french: Le silence éternel de ces espaces infinis m'effraie.
sample_passages.english: The eternal silence of these infinite spaces frightens me.
sample_passages.notes: One of the most famous lines in French philosophy. Note the subjunctive is not used here; the indicative 'effraie' expresses a fact, not a doubt.

sample_passages.french: Ce que nous prenons pour des vertus n'est souvent qu'un assemblage de diverses actions et de divers intérêts que la fortune ou notre industrie savent arranger.
sample_passages.english: What we take for virtues is often only an assemblage of various actions and various interests that fortune or our industry know how to arrange.
sample_passages.notes: A characteristic maxim: cynical, precise, paradoxical. The verb 'savent' is plural, agreeing with 'fortune ou notre industrie'.

capstone_prep.sight_translation: Practice translating fifty-word passages from Pascal and La Rochefoucauld without notes.
capstone_prep.parsing: Identify and parse verb forms, noun cases, and pronoun references in complex sentences.
capstone_prep.composition: Render five English sentences in French, using vocabulary and structures from the moralist texts.
capstone_prep.oral_component: Prepare a one-hundred-word passage from Pascal or La Rochefoucauld to read aloud. Answer five questions about its language and content.
